ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 18.3 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 15.7 km, a deviation of 2.60 km (deviation_pct 16.6). That exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, so under POL-RD-22 the deviation is outside tolerance and the trip is not protected by any tolerance finding.

The route actually driven is confirmed independently of the driver's account: the trace runs along Tampines Expressway (TPE) from 14:18:41 and then along Braddell Road from 14:29:41, rejoining the recommended route at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41 — the driver left the recommended PIE routing at the Pasir Ris Drive 3 / TPE slip road at 14:18:56 and did not return for roughly 22 minutes. The GPS trace identifies which route was taken and when; under POL-RD-22 it is not used to re-measure the distance, but it confirms the deviation event the trip record records.

No traffic justification exists for this reroute. The only advisory in the record is a ROADWORK on Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas after Tampines Avenue 10 exit, with a validity window of 2026-09-05T23:00:00 to 2026-09-06T05:00:00. The derived facts record overlaps_trip_window as false and justifies_reroute as false, and the reason states that POL-RD-23 is not satisfied because the advisory's active window falls outside the trip window (this trip ran 14:16–14:42). POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that both intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; a driver's bare assertion of roadworks, with no such data, does not justify the reroute.

Even if traffic had justified the reroute, the driver never told the rider. The chat log is contiguous and carries 0 messages, the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, and the trip record's messages_during_trip is an empty list; there is no call recording in the record. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation, and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. The rider's own account — that the driver 'never said why' — is therefore the only account on contact, and it is unrebutted by any message.

The refund follows from the matrix. With the deviation over 1 km and no traffic justification, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 2.60 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.87 SGD, rounded to the cent. A PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.87 SGD is the monetary remedy this clause provides.

The rider is currently carrying the disputed charge: payment_status is CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 and total_charged is 21.56 SGD, so nothing has been returned. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION would preserve that present state and leave the contested excess distance fare on the rider, whereas a PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the trip's charge. The rider's win here is a ruling that takes the disputed charge off the rider.

This case is one the AI may decide. The dispute value is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags is 0 on the authority record, matched by EV-RPROF-05015 and EV-DPROF-05015), and no safety flag is set. POL-RD-25's additional limb, the 2 km ceiling, is not applied — thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — so it does not force escalation. Nothing here requires the case to be held for a human rather than decided in the rider's favour.

The most this trip can return under POL-RD-24 is the excess distance fare, and that figure is 1.87 SGD. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation on the platform's recorded distances: 18.3 km actual minus 15.7 km recommended = 2.60 km, not on the sparse trace. POL-RD-24 prices the excess at the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, with no surge and no other component: 2.60 x 0.72 = 1.87 SGD. The rider's demand for 6.00 SGD overshoots the policy measure by 4.13 SGD; that 4.13 SGD, and the rest of the metered charge, stays with the driver.

The deviation of 2.60 km is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance, no refund' rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 are closed, and row (a) needs the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the empty chat log forecloses. That leaves rows (b) and (d), and both pay exactly the same excess distance fare. Whichever of the two the judge takes, the rider recovers 1.87 SGD, not the 6.00 SGD claimed: no row of POL-RD-24 lets the rider recover more than the measured excess.

The chat log carries 0 messages and the trip record carries no in-app calls, so the driver did not give recorded notice of the deviation under POL-RD-21. But that lapse carries no money of its own: POL-RD-24 pays the same excess distance fare of 1.87 SGD in row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed) as in row (d) (not traffic-justified), and it excludes any time-fare adjustment for the 3.7 minutes of extra running. The silence cannot be used to enlarge the refund beyond the measured excess.

This case fits POL-RD-24 row (d) and is decided on the money, not pushed to a human. The dispute value is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 2 km escalation limb is switched off because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false. Every artifact the row needs - trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and the traffic advisory - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no POL-GEN-26 open question to escalate.

ruling.explanation:
Both accounts agree on the shape of this dispute, and the record resolves it. The deviation is measured under POL-RD-22 on the platform's recorded distances, not on the sparse trace: the trip record shows 18.3 km actually driven against 15.7 km on the recommended route, a deviation of 2.60 km (16.6%), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance, but it confirms which route was taken — the vehicle left the recommended Pan-Island Expressway routing at the Pasir Ris Drive 3 / TPE slip road at 14:18:56, ran the TPE and then Braddell Road, and rejoined at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41.

On traffic justification (POL-RD-23), the driver's explanation does not hold. The only advisory in the record is a ROADWORK on the PIE (towards Tuas) after Tampines Avenue 10 exit, and its validity window is 2026-09-05 23:00 to 2026-09-06 05:00 — the trip ran 14:16–14:42, so the advisory does not overlap the trip window and does not justify the reroute. POL-RD-23 is explicit that a driver's bare assertion of traffic, with no overlapping traffic data, does not justify a reroute. The driver's statement of roadworks is therefore noted but not accepted as a justification.

On notice (POL-RD-21), the chat log is contiguous with 0 messages, the trip record's in-app calls and messages_during_trip are empty, and there is no call recording in the record. A verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. The driver did not give recorded notice of the deviation.

Applying the POL-RD-24 matrix: the deviation is over tolerance, so rows (c) and (e) are closed; row (a) requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the empty chat log forecloses; and the reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case falls in row (d) — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 2.60 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.87 SGD, rounded to the cent. This is the whole monetary remedy the matrix provides; it is not the 6.00 SGD claimed, because POL-RD-24 returns the excess distance fare and not the trip fare, and it is not a NO_ACTION, because the deviation exceeded tolerance with no traffic justification. The rider is carrying the charge (total_charged 21.56 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.87 SGD returns that part of the trip's charge.

On who decides: the contested amount is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag and no safety flag is set, so the AI ruling is final on that clause; POL-RD-25's own 0.80 confidence requirement is met, and its extra 2 km limb is switched off because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false. Every artifact this ruling rests on — the trip record, the GPS trace, the fare breakdown and the traffic advisory — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no fact is left unestablished and POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
